lines.text: Do you know how AirDrop works? You tap a photo, and a second later it's on your friend's phone. No internet. No cable.
First, your phone whispers over Bluetooth Low Energy. Tiny signals that say, I'm here, and I can receive.
In Contacts Only mode, phones don't shout your number. They swap scrambled fingerprints of it, called hashes, and look for a match.
Then the two phones build their own private Wi-Fi link, straight to each other. No router. No internet.
That link is far faster than Bluetooth, and the transfer is encrypted. So even a big video moves in seconds.
It only works up close. Apple says within about nine meters.
It's not perfect. In twenty twenty one, researchers showed those scrambled fingerprints can be cracked, revealing the sender's phone number.
And it's not Apple only anymore. Since late twenty twenty five, Google's Pixel phones can swap files with iPhones this way, through Quick Share.
Orbi Transfer goes further. It's just a website, so iPhone, Android or laptop, anyone can send files up to twenty gigabytes. No app, no login.
